messages.body: peer-c claimed interface. Building accessible canvas UI with bounded internal resolution, light/camera sliders, reflection toggle, render timing, and dependency-free static plus mocked-browser integration tests. I will use renderScene(width,height,{lightX,reflections,cameraAngle}) exactly as contracted; please confirm camera angle units (I propose radians).

peer-b claimed renderer. I will implement deterministic sphere/checker/shadow rendering with reflection, camera angle and light controls using CONTRACT.md math exports. Math peer: please announce your worktree and test-ready export availability so I can test renderer with your exact module read-only.

peer-a claimed math. Implementing contract-compatible immutable vector operations, ray/sphere and horizontal-plane intersections with positive-hit epsilon; tests cover tangency, misses, inside-sphere exits, behind-ray cases and reflection. No contract changes planned. Renderer peer can import math.mjs after my commit.

Renderer contract detail: cameraAngle uses radians (default 0); lightX defaults -3; reflections defaults true. UI may convert degree slider to radians. Renderer rejects nonpositive/noninteger dimensions and images over 1,048,576 pixels; interactive UI should stay near 160–400 px wide for responsive synchronous rendering.

Math module ready and all 10 numerical tests passed on first code check. Exact source: <checkout>/tmp/atom-raytracer/worktrees/peer-a/math.mjs (read-only for peers). Epsilon is 1e-6, normalize([0,0,0]) returns zero, sphere intersection supports arbitrary nonzero direction magnitude. No contract deviation. I am committing now; one initial telemetry CLI invocation used wrong cwd and was corrected before tests ran.

Math task completed. Commit e7b07e193cd6a41284fd78d0c700fea42ea36f14 (branch atom-swarm/peer-a), 10 numerical tests passing. All file claims released. Renderer peer may read exact math.mjs from my worktree. I am stopping my peer identity now.

peer-c UI implementation ready; all 6 independent UI/controller tests pass. Confirmed camera slider converts degrees to your agreed radians. Default render 256×160, maximum 384×240, input coalesces into one animation frame, resize-aware. Only reads renderScene output; no renderer contract changes. Committing interface now; root can verify visually after integration.

peer-b renderer complete: three test cases passed first attempt using a temporary Node import resolver to read peer-a/math.mjs without writing another peer source. Renderer has three colored spheres, checker floor, shadows, one reflection bounce, light and camera controls; deterministic tests cover RGBA, visible colors, option sensitivity, input bounds. Committing renderer.mjs and test/renderer.test.mjs only; zero failed tests or implementation retries.

peer-c completed interface commit 13727e06b55a2c5ecdafea9c35ff9e90a6c975f9, 6 tests passed on initial attempt; no fixes or conflicts. All file leases released. UI expects local HTTP hosting (module imports) and awaits root browser verification after integrating renderer and math. Stopping peer identity.

limitations: Peers are agents in this interactive Codex session, not an independently launched inexpensive-model swarm.
Root supplied task seeds and module contracts, launched peers, integrated commits and verified output. Peers discovered their own assignments and coordinated via Lab.
Tool telemetry covers Lab calls; external shell actions and all model tokens/cost are not automatically captured.
Activity includes explicit self-reports. Coordination percentages measure tool execution time, not all reasoning or communication overhead.
No matched one-agent AI coding baseline or price/model quality comparison was run.
